title: A guide to agentic AI platforms and how they benefit B2B support teams
summary: Learn what agentic AI platforms are and which capabilities matter most. Plus, explore top solutions and see how Pylon helps B2B support teams work smarter.
body_markdown:
Despite all the concerns about AI replacing humans, the pattern in most industries is more nuanced. In fields like software dev, healthcare, legal, and customer support, companies are using AI to improve how their people work, not to automate those roles completely.


At Pylon, we’ve seen this pattern with our own customers: Building[strong B2B relationships](https://www.usepylon.com/blog/how-to-build-relationship-with-customers) calls for workflows that bring AI and human efforts together. An agentic AI platform can help support teams work faster by researching customer issues, accessing account context, suggesting responses, and taking autonomous actions. Meanwhile, your team keeps full control over one-on-one interactions and account-level management.


In this guide, we’ll explain what an agentic AI platform is and what capabilities you should look for. We’ll also cover the types of tools on the market and how to choose the best platform for[B2B customer support](https://www.usepylon.com/blog/b2b-customer-service-best-practices-strategies) .


## What’s an agentic AI platform?


Agent runbook view from Pylon


In a traditional support platform, your team works through customer requests one at a time. They research answers, coordinate with other teams, resolve issues, and respond to customers, maybe with the help of[some basic automation](https://www.usepylon.com/blog/customer-support-automation) and a chatbot.


With an agentic AI platform, your support team can[direct AI agents](https://www.usepylon.com/blog/how-to-use-ai-agents) to do some of that work independently. For example, if a B2B customer asks for help with a software integration, an AI agent can investigate the issue. The agent accesses connected context, like the company’s[knowledge base](https://www.usepylon.com/blog/knowledge-base-guide) and previous support tickets, to find a solution.


Then, it can present next steps to your team along with a draft response for the customer. At that point, your team can either accept the suggestions, direct the AI agent to investigate further, or take over personally if the issue is especially complex or delicate.


This shift from doing the work by hand to orchestrating repeatable workflows reflects how AI is used in software development. While devs used to write and review every line of code, they can now use LLMs like Claude Code to do much of the time-consuming work. This saves time and lets them focus on more high-level tasks, like deciding what the code should do and perfecting the AI outputs.


An agentic platform makes it possible to direct AI to perform complex workflows, even if no one on your team is a coding expert. You give instructions in natural language, and you get helpful context and suggestions the same way. And quality platforms also offer data access tools and other guardrails to help you[set up AI agents](https://www.usepylon.com/blog/how-to-set-up-ai-agents) safely.


## Core features to look for in an agentic AI platform


Some of what you’ll need depends on your[use cases](https://www.usepylon.com/blog/agentic-ai-use-cases) , but here’s what any good agentic AI tool for B2B support should have:


- **Multi-agent structure.** You should be able to direct different AI agents to complete distinct tasks. For example, you could use one agent to answer customer questions directly using knowledge base content, while another agent[investigates issues in the background](https://www.usepylon.com/ai-agents/automations) based on automated triggers.
- **Deep system integration.** Look for a platform you can easily connect with your knowledge base, CRM, billing tools, and other operational systems. The more data your AI agent can access, the better it is at both investigation and autonomous action.
- **Oversight and auditing.** Make sure you can see what agents are doing and control what they’re able to access. The system should also flag any unexpected behaviors, so you can fix those issues before they affect customers.
- **Strong governance.** Choose a platform that lets you specify exactly what AI agents can handle autonomously and when humans need to review or approve their actions. You could let an AI agent respond to simple queries about how your product works, but have it escalate to your support team for complex troubleshooting.
- **Flexible model support.** AI models change often, so look for a platform that keeps up with new technology and connects to your other AI tools through the[Model Context Protocol](https://docs.usepylon.com/pylon-docs/integrations/pylon-mcp) .
- **Scalable, repeatable workflows.** As your AI agents work on customer issues, they’ll often perform the same workflows again and again. Look for a platform that lets you[define repeat workflows or skills](https://www.usepylon.com/ai-agents/skills) , so the AI doesn’t have to start from scratch each time.


## Common types of agentic AI systems


Agentic AI includes a range of different technologies, from broad-use platforms to niche systems designed for specific tasks. These are the main categories:


- **General-purpose enterprise platforms** are flexible systems that help you build AI agents for various business functions, then organize them all in one place. Examples include Salesforce Agentforce and Microsoft Copilot Studio.
- **Purpose-built agentic platforms** are highly specialized systems that build and manage AI agents for a particular industry or use case. These tools trade the breadth of a general-purpose platform for depth in a single domain. Good examples include[Pylon for B2B customer support](https://www.usepylon.com/blog/pylon-becomes-the-agentic-support-platform) teams, Harvey for legal firms, and Rogo for finance companies.
- **Developer frameworks** allow coders to create AI agents that write and review code autonomously, so devs can focus on designing applications. Some popular tools in this category are CrewAI and AutoGen.
- **No-code automation tools** like Zapier and n8n help business users automate basic, repetitive workflows by building AI agents using intuitive interfaces.


## Choosing the best agentic AI platform for B2B customer support


Ask AI view from Pylon


General-purpose agentic AI tools work well for simple, large-scale task execution. But B2B customer support calls for a more purpose-built solution. Teams need to manage customer relationships with multiple stakeholders across[various support channels](https://www.usepylon.com/blog/practical-guide-to-omnichannel-support) . And they need to collaborate with other teams while drawing on deep account context from long-term relationships.


Pylon’s agentic support platform is designed to meet the specific needs of B2B customer support operations. It comes with AI agents built for different support workflows, allowing teams to stop investigating tickets and start overseeing accounts.


Here’s a look at how Pylon’s AI agents and features work together:


- **Assist Agent** answers questions and investigates issues based on your instructions. You give this agent access to product and customer context, and it suggests solutions and drafts responses.
- **Automations** use triggers to investigate issues as they arrive, pulling context from docs, past tickets, and connected tools. That way, your support team has what it needs to help customers.

- **Slack Agent** makes it easy for your team to get information about your product and customers by tagging @Pylon in Slack.
- **Skills** are reusable workflows you define using natural language, then make available to both AI agents and your team to promote consistency.

## FAQ


### How can I get started with agentic AI?


You can use an agentic AI platform to define agent behavior in plain language, often as reusable Skills. Start with a single repetitive task, configure an AI agent to work on it, and expand the scope only after that single workflow is working reliably.


### Can beginners learn agentic AI?


Yes. With an agentic AI platform, you can direct AI agents and customize workflows without needing a coding or technical background. Instead of diving into code, you simply need to understand your workflow well enough to hand the right piece to an agent, then test and iterate.


### What’s the difference between generative AI and agentic AI?


Generative AI creates content like text, images, or code in response to a prompt. Agentic AI goes a step further and takes actions like looking something up, updating a record, or completing a multi-step task.


### Can you explain agentic AI in a simple way?


Agentic AI is a form of artificial intelligence built around autonomous decision making and action. Instead of just responding to a command or analyzing data, agentic AI can set a goal, plan the steps to reach it, and carry those steps out with minimal human involvement.
